And he stretched it forth: and his hand vvas restored. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=11}}† And they vvere replenished vvith madnes: and they communed one with an other vvhat they might doe to {{sc|Iesvs}}.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Bartlemewes day.}}And it came to passe in those daies, he vvent forth into the mountaine to pray, and he passed {{sup|‖}} the vvhole night in the prayer of God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10, 1. Mr. 3, 13. 6, 7. Lu. 9, 1.''}}* And vvhen day vvas come, he called his Disciples: and he chose tvvelue of them (v{{sup|‖}} vhom also he named ''Apostles'') {{verse|chapter=6|verse=14}}† {{sup|‖}} Simon vvhom he surnamed Peter, and Andrevv his brother, Iames and Iohn, Philippe and Bartholomevv, {{verse|chapter=6|verse=15}}† Matthevv and Thomas, Iames of Alphæus and Simon that is called Zelótes, {{verse|chapter=6|verse=16}}† and Iude of Iames, and Iudas Iscariote vvhich vvas the traitour. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Alholowes eue. And for many Martyrs.}}And descending vvith them he stoode in a plaine place, and the multitude of his Disciples, and a very great companie of people from al Ievvrie and Hierusalem: and the sea coast both of Tyre and Sidon, {{verse|chapter=6|verse=18}}† vvhich vvere come to heare him, and to be healed of their maladies. And they that vvere vexed of vncleane spirits, vvere cured. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=19}}† And al the multitude {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''See S. Mar. Annot. c. 5, 28.''}}* sought to touch him, because vertue vvent forth from him, and healed al.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=20}}† And he lifting vp his eies vpon his Disciples, said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 5, 2. 6, 7.''}}* Blessed are ye poore: for yours is the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=21}}† Blessed are you that novv are an hungred: because you shal be filled. Blessed are you that novv doe vveepe: because you shal laugh. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=22}}† Blessed shal you be vvhen men shal hate you, and vvhen they shal separate you, and vpbraide you, and abandon your name as euil, for the sonne of mans sake. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=23}}† {{sup|‖}} Be glad in that day and reioyce: for behold, your revvard is much in heauen. ⊣ for according to these things did their fathers to the Prophets. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=24}}† But wo to you that are riche, because you haue your consolation. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=25}}† VVo to you that are filled: because you shal be hungrie. VVo to you that novv doe laugh: because you shal mourne and vveepe. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† VVo, vvhen al men {{sup|‖}} shal blesse you. for according to these things did their fathers to the false-Prophets.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† But to you I say that doe heare, Loue your enemies, doe good to them that hate you. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}}† Blesse them that curse you, and pray for them that calumniate you. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}}† And he that striketh thee on the cheeke, offer also the other. And from him that taketh avvay from thee thy robe, prohibit not thy coate also. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ That is, to euery one iustly asking. For that which is vniustly asked, may be iustly denied. ''Aug. li. 1. c. 40. de Serm. Do. in monte''.}}∷ to euery one that asketh thee, giue: and of him<noinclude>{{rh|||that}}</noinclude>
